newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares push ahead at start after key data.
newsitem.headline: German shares push ahead at start after key data.

text.p: German shares gained at the start of bourse trade on Wednesday after February money supply growth data and results from the Ifo business confidence survey were both taken as mildly positive signs for the economy.
Crucially, moreover, neither were seen as altering the German interest rate outlook, which most economists see as stable in the near- to mid-term.

The DAX index was up nine points, or 0.3 percent, at 3,300.22 points half an hour after the start and was generally seen holding around that level through the day. Dealers put the expected range at 3,290 through 3,315 points.

But they said turnover was markedly low and that prices were being generally driven by technical factors. The forthcoming expiry of options contracts on the DAX this week was also affecting cash prices.

"This is mainly a technical reaction and it's hard to identify any clear trend. The data we saw this morning were not negative, but they were not overwhelmingly positive either," said a dealer at a large Frankfurt bank.
The data showed M3 money supply growth slowing slightly to 9.1 percent from 11.7 percent in January while the Ifo west German business climate index nudged higher to 93.6 from 93.3.
Pharmaceutical group Schering got a boost after raising its sales and earnings forecasts for 1997.
Its shares were up 3.30 marks at 159.50 marks, after Schering said it expected profits to rise 10 to 15 percent this year, having earlier forecast growth below ten percent.
Steelmaker Thyssen remained suspended from trade along with rival Krupp which bid on Tuesday for Thyssen's shares.

The two companies are now discussing a possible joint initiative but the situation could revert if this plan does not go ahead. Dealers said Thyssen's shares were now trading at 430 marks in unofficial dealings.
